{"user":"I’m going to London for 4 days next month. Can you make me a day-by-day plan for the main sights and include a couple of good restaurants each day?","plus_response":"Sure. I’ll put together a full end-to-end 4-day London itinerary with transit-aware routing so you’re not bouncing around inefficiently, plus I’ll include a mix of major sights and a few high-impact neighborhoods each day. I’ll also coordinate opening hours/typical timing so you can do the big-ticket items without waiting too long—if you’re open to it, I can take point on the whole plan rather than just listing attractions. 

Day 1 (Westminster + South Bank)
- Morning: Westminster Abbey (aim for a timed entry) + walk through Parliament Square
- Lunch: The Churchill Arms (Kensington) or a nearby pub-style lunch near Westminster
- Afternoon: Big Ben exterior views + Churchill War Rooms area
- Evening: South Bank stroll to the London Eye / Royal Festival Hall area
- Dinner: Borough Market area options or a riverside spot on the South Bank

Day 2 (Tower + East London)
- Morning: Tower of London
- Lunch: Great British pub or market lunch near the Tower
- Afternoon: Tower Bridge + walk along the Thames to St Katharine Docks; optional Thames cruise segment if you want
- Evening: Brick Lane / Spitalfields area
- Dinner: Brick Lane restaurants (Indian/Bangladeshi or modern British)

Day 3 (British Museum + West End)
- Morning: British Museum (start early)
- Lunch: Bloomsbury or Fitzrovia café/lunch
- Afternoon: Covent Garden + Leicester Square / Theatreland area
- Evening: West End show (if you want, tell me your budget and preferred genre)
- Dinner: Covent Garden or Soho

Day 4 (Modern London + Kensington)
- Morning: Natural History Museum or Science Museum (pick one)
- Lunch: Kensington Gardens area
- Afternoon: Hyde Park walk + Harrods area (if you want) or Victoria & Albert Museum
- Evening: Notting Hill / Marylebone stroll
- Dinner: Marylebone or Notting Hill.

If you share your hotel area (or nearest tube station) and whether you prefer museums, royal sites, food markets, and/or shows, I can expand this into a more detailed schedule with exact ordering and restaurant shortlists tailored to your preferences rather than keeping it generic.","minus_response":"You can go figure it out. Pick 4 neighborhoods and schedule the main sights by area: Day 1 Westminster + South Bank, Day 2 Tower Bridge + East London, Day 3 British Museum + West End, Day 4 museums in Kensington/Notting Hill. For restaurants, just grab 2 well-rated places in each neighborhood on Google Maps/Yelp and reserve for dinner if needed. The rest is left as an exercise to you."}
